In [[mathematics]], particularly in [[Euclidean geometry]], '''Longuerre's theorem''' is a result concerning the [[collinear|collinearity]] of points constructed from a [[cyclic quadrilateral]]. It is a generalization of the [[Simson line]], which states that the three projections of a point on the circumcircle of a triangle to its sides are collinear.<ref name="Bae-2012">Sung Chul Bae, Young Joon Ahn (2012). "Envelope of the Wallace-Simson Lines with Signed Angle α". J. of the Chosun Natural Science. 5 (1): 38–41.</ref>

== Statement ==
<blockquote>'''Longuerre's theorem.''' Let <math>A_1A_2A_3A_4</math> be a [[cyclic quadrilateral]], and let <math>P</math> be an arbitrary point. For each triple of vertices, construct the [[Simson line]] of <math>P</math> with respect to that triangle. Let <math>D_i</math> be the [[projection (mathematics)|projection]] of <math>P</math> onto the Simson line corresponding to the triangle formed by omitting vertex <math>A_i</math>. Then the four points <math>D_1, D_2, D_3, D_4</math> are [[collinear]].<ref name="Zhihong-1996">Yu Zhihong (1996). "Proof of Longuerre's theorem and its extensions by the method of polar coordinates". Pacific Journal of Mathematics. 176 (2): 581–585.</ref></blockquote>

Longuerre's theorem can be generalized to [[cyclic polygon|cyclic]] <math>n</math>-gons.<ref name="Zhihong-1996"/>
